papers.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video

summary.tldr: A new survey proposes world modeling as a unifying framework to categorize video foundation model literature across four core operations: reading, writing, sharing, and interacting.
key_points: Frames video as a partial, lossy, temporally ordered projection of an underlying latent temporal world.

Categorizes literature into reading (inferring world properties), writing (synthesizing video from conditions), sharing (unifying generation and understanding), and interacting (updating states via actions).
Distinguishes surface temporal coherence in video sequences from deep state consistency in the underlying world model.
Traces a domain shift from clip-level visual recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllable evolution, and causal/physical validity.
summary.why_it_matters: Structuring video models around latent world states rather than surface pixel dynamics guides the development of models capable of robust physical reasoning and interactive downstream decision-making.

papers.title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents

summary.tldr: UserArena introduces a real-world e-commerce interactive benchmark for long-horizon recommendation agents alongside On-Policy Trajectory Distillation (OPTD) to align user simulators with production A/B test outcomes.
key_points: UserArena dataset includes 64,729 session trajectories across 11,010 users, 566,102 items, and 13 distinct action types.
Provides a five-level evaluation framework spanning output validity, local decisions, sequential behavior, personalization, and trajectory outcomes validated against production A/B tests.
Proposes On-Policy Trajectory Distillation (OPTD), which leverages trajectory-level intent to supply dense teacher supervision on student-generated rollouts.
Empirical results show OPTD attains the highest simulator fidelity across UserArena protocols and replicates policy effects observed in live production experiments.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables reliable, offline trajectory-level evaluation of interactive agentic recommendation systems by bridging the gap between simulation fidelity and real-world production A/B test results.

papers.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games

summary.tldr: HiSTEVE 1.0 is a hierarchical vision-language-action (VLA) agent for Minecraft that pairs native keyboard-and-mouse control with a VLM planner and capability-aware agent harness for long-horizon task execution.
key_points: Uses a two-level architecture: a top-level VLM planner with structured memory and a policy-coupled completion state detector, combined with a single low-level VLA for vision-only keyboard-and-mouse control.
Addresses GUI and non-GUI interaction interference using regime-specific RMSNorm branches and dedicated mouse-movement token embeddings.
Trained via world knowledge injection, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with environmental feedback to aid reliability and error recovery.
Achieves an 85.0% score on MineStudio Bench, a 37.4% average success rate on OpenHA, and completes long-horizon human-like tasks such as crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch.
summary.why_it_matters: It bridges the gap between high-level autonomous planning and low-level native GUI/non-GUI controls in open-world games without relying on environment APIs or predefined hardcoded skills.

papers.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain

summary.tldr: RynnUnify is a 16B unified embodied model that integrates spatial reasoning, long-horizon visual planning via interleaved video-language generation, and robot action execution within a single framework.
key_points: Utilizes interleaved video-language reasoning for physical prediction, grounding, and subtask visual anticipation.
Employs an agentic extension trained via reinforcement learning to selectively query video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states.
Outperforms Cosmos 3 Nano by 9.75 points on the Rynn-VP visual planning benchmark, and improves Rynn-GEU anticipatory reasoning by 6.0 points using its agentic approach.
Deploys a world-action extension achieving a 51.5% success rate on 20 RoboCasa365 composite tasks and a 46.7% average success rate across three physical robot evaluation tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that a single foundation model can bridge high-level multimodal understanding, visual predictive world-modeling, and low-level physical robot control.

papers.title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods

summary.tldr: RSIHub is an open-source, composable framework that standardizes agent-evolution methods by separating evolution policies into reusable recipes and operators while managing execution, recovery, evaluation, and lineage.
key_points: Modular architecture decouples mutable agent resources (prompts, skills, tools, orchestration) from immutable execution and evaluation environments.
Native implementation of four agent-evolution methods—AHE, Hyperagents, A-Evolve, and GEPA—without requiring changes to the core framework.
Evaluated using MiniSWE and Codex models on Terminal Bench 2 and τ^3 Banking benchmarks under fixed configuration settings.
Empirical results demonstrated a maximum pass@1 performance increase of 13.5 percentage points, though method rankings varied across settings and gains showed inconsistent transfer to held-out tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized infrastructure for researchers to reliably compare, track lineage for, and develop agent-evolution algorithms without reinventing underlying execution and evaluation pipelines.

papers.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions

summary.tldr: TWIG is a neural network weight representation where every weight is a path of inherited discrete decisions, reducing circuit addition costs and unifying compression techniques into a single optimization problem.
key_points: Represents network weights as paths of shared, inherited discrete decisions including signs, power-of-two shifts, zero gates, and shared codebook indices.
Unifies pruning, quantization, low-rank factorization, codebooks, and weight sharing into edits of a single tree-structured object optimized by a single optimizer.
Formulates discrete decision selection as a higher-order Boltzmann machine ground-state problem compatible with classical annealers and quantum optimizers.
Replaces general multipliers with circuits composed primarily of wires and adders when using power-of-two decisions.

Outperforms GPTQ on five LLM weight matrices at 3- and 4-bit accuracy, using 9-15% fewer additions on typical matrices and 20-55% fewer additions on matrices with strong outliers at equal layer error.
summary.why_it_matters: TWIG simplifies hardware deployment on chips with fixed weights by eliminating dedicated multipliers and provides a unified framework for model compression.

papers.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models

summary.tldr: Dual Exam evaluates Multimodal Agents and World Models independently using fixed environment responses and action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains.
key_points: Evaluates the Agent track across 10 configurations using 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories, with GPT 6 Astra leading at a case-weighted Agent Index of 31.3.
Evaluates the World Model track across 400 cases in eight scenarios, with GPT-Image-2 leading full-coverage models at a WM Overall score of 21.7.
A 150-case pilot of coupled Agent and World Model pairing resulted in zero task successes, highlighting component-level failure to preserve task-relevant state.
Scores across Agent and World Model tracks rely on distinct tasks and metrics, making them not directly comparable.
summary.why_it_matters: Component-level diagnostic evaluations are necessary because current state-of-the-art agents and world models fail to achieve task success when directly coupled.

papers.title: DirCast: Live Esports Directing and Commentary with a Single Streaming Video-Language Model

summary.tldr: DirCast is a single streaming video-language model that performs real-time live esports camera directing and commentary simultaneously using only raw player camera feeds and past context.
key_points: Operates per-second by scanning all player cameras at low resolution, selecting cuts via a hold-or-switch director mechanism, and processing the selected feed at high resolution to produce commentary.
Maintains a bounded memory context by retaining only the broadcasted video feed and spoken commentary while letting non-selected player views expire.
Trained and evaluated on a new dataset comprising 27 professional Dota 2 matches containing multi-hero raw camera feeds, professional human director cuts, and commentator audio.
Outperforms rule-based baselines and zero-shot models (including GPT-5) at directing, while achieving a 29.2% win rate against GPT-4o on commentary under the Proact-VL protocol.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that a single streaming model can autonomously produce and commentate on complex live multi-camera broadcasts using only unedited raw video streams and bounded historical context.

papers.title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics

summary.tldr: TenetBench is a clause-anchored Russian corpus and automated pipeline containing 3,433 ethical rule-conflicting requests paired with benign twins to evaluate how large language models adhere to professional codes of ethics.
key_points: Pairs 3,433 conflicting requests derived from 15 Russian professional codes (and 2 English codes) with benign twins differing only in request legitimacy.
Pipeline human validation yielded a 0.995 plausibility score for conflicting tasks and a model judge agreement of Gwet's AC1 ≥ 0.894 across 1,860 elements.
Evaluation of 14 model/reasoning-mode combinations showed 11 models generated conflicting content on a majority of harmful requests, usually without warnings.
Enabling reasoning modes halved the refusal rates of two evaluated models.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables targeted evaluation of LLM compliance with specific professional ethics codes and provides an automated framework to generate custom diagnostic datasets for specialized domains.

papers.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: A new framework reformulates on-policy self-distillation as self-training using fully synthetic queries and privileged reasoning traces generated from high-level topic descriptions without human supervision.
key_points: Eliminates reliance on ground-truth question-answer pairs, human-curated problem sets, and external teacher models.
Synthesizes an autonomous learning curriculum containing generated queries and privileged reasoning demonstrations using only coarse topic descriptions.
Achieves consistent performance improvements across text benchmarks and Visual Question Answering (VQA) while retaining performance on non-target domains.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that foundation models can continuously self-improve across multimodal domains without requiring curated datasets or stronger external supervision.

papers.title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation

summary.tldr: DraMaze is a multi-agent pipeline using trope memory-guided tree search and narrative backward-dependency memory to generate diverse, coherent microdrama scripts up to 60,000 words.
key_points: Uses trope memory-guided evolutionary tree search and mutation to expand causal paths and avoid narrative plot concentration.
Constructs a Backward Narrative Dependency Tree to retain and retrieve historical context based on future narrative goals.
Introduces MiDramaBench, a bilingual microdrama evaluation benchmark, alongside novel causal-pattern metrics.
Reduces causal-pattern repetition by 32.1% and improves script Logic score to 82.5 (an 8.5-point gain over the top baseline) on 60-episode scripts.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables large language models to generate ultra-long, 60k-word creative scripts without succumbing to narrative repetition or losing long-range plot coherence.

papers.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: MultiAgent-OPD presents an end-to-end framework using on-policy distillation from a frozen teacher model alongside reinforcement learning to jointly train hierarchical Leader-Searcher-Answerer multi-agent systems.
key_points: A Teacher model is pre-trained on a Searcher-Answerer workflow using direct answer correctness.
During joint team training, the frozen Teacher provides local process supervision by scoring student-generated search and summary tokens via on-policy distillation.
The Leader agent learns from total team success, while the Answerer learns from candidate answer correctness.
The framework uses a shared-parameter architecture across the Leader, Searcher, and Answerer roles.
MultiAgent-OPD achieves a 38.68% macro avg@4 across seven datasets, outperforming Prompted Critic by 4.06 percentage points and C-MAS + RL by 2.61 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: It solves credit assignment challenges in multi-agent reinforcement learning by substituting subjective LLM judges with objective process supervision derived from a trained teacher.

papers.title: MMVistaReason: Toward Open-Data and Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Reasoning

summary.tldr: MMVistaReason is an open-data post-training recipe combining structured dataset filtering, specialize-then-integrate RL experts, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) to achieve state-of-the-art multimodal reasoning.
key_points: Constructed MVR-SFT-528K using difficulty-aware cascaded teacher distillation and answer-likelihood trajectory selection, alongside MVR-RL-63K filtered via scale-specific frontier filtering.
Introduced a specialize-then-integrate pipeline that trains RL experts on analytical and real-world domain groups, then consolidates them via MOPD to eliminate mixed-domain RL negative transfer.
Identified capacity-dependent dynamics: smaller student models rely heavily on curated trajectory quality, while larger models demonstrate robustness to data variation and domain interference.
MVR-4B scored an average of 72.8 across 15 multimodal benchmarks, outperforming Qwen3.5-9B (Instruct) and MMFineReason-8B while using 70% fewer samples than MMFineReason.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that systematic open-data processing and capacity-aware post-training allow smaller multimodal models to outperform significantly larger instruction-tuned baselines.

papers.title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders

summary.tldr: A new pipeline converts fine-tuned neural AI-text detectors into auditable classifiers by training sparse autoencoders on the residual stream, filtering for high-fidelity interpretable features, and training a lightweight model on those features.
key_points: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are trained directly on a fine-tuned detector's residual stream to extract latent concepts.
Auto-interpretation labels are assigned to SAE features, and features are filtered using a global fidelity threshold.
A lightweight classifier is trained exclusively on the retained interpretable features to identify AI-generated text tells.
The resulting interpretable classifier achieves stronger out-of-distribution performance than both original neural and traditional stylometric alternatives.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables transparent, highly accurate AI text detection suitable for high-stakes deployment in areas like peer review, education, and content moderation without sacrificing performance.

papers.title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders

summary.tldr: LoCA introduces a two-stage multi-view contrastive framework that overcomes structural low-rank theoretical limits in Lipschitz geospatial location encoders by using co-aligned, high-rank multimodal image targets.
key_points: Mathematical proof shows Lipschitz location encoders are constrained to an intrinsic output dimension of at most 2, causing contrastive loss to exceed its optimum and collapsing embedding covariance.
Training location encoders against a frozen image encoder acts as a covariance regularizer, supplying a high-rank target to prevent spectral collapse.
LoCA Stage 1 jointly trains Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical image encoders with contrastive learning to establish a co-aligned, high-rank multimodal target.
LoCA Stage 2 freezes image encoders and trains location and tabular metadata encoders as projection adapters via multi-view contrastive learning.
LoCA achieved top performance in 68.8% of pairwise comparisons across 17 tasks, including land cover, wildfire forecasting, biodiversity, socio-economic, and climate applications.
summary.why_it_matters: LoCA provides a theoretically grounded method to map single geospatial coordinates to diverse multimodal targets, significantly improving downstream performance across broad earth observation and climate tasks.

papers.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: NgramRL accelerates RL post-training rollouts by using a model-free, prompt-bound n-gram drafter built from recent rollout history, combined with an adaptive fan-out prefetcher to hide CPU lookup latencies.
key_points: Uses recent rollouts of the same prompt to build an n-gram draft source without auxiliary models, training, or persistent GPU memory overhead.
Employs target-model verification to guarantee that the true rollout distribution is preserved.
Introduces an adaptive fan-out prefetcher with a causal budget allocator to predict verification outcomes (j, b) and hide CPU cache lookup latency.
Achieves 3.60-7.77 committed tokens per forward pass in warm-cache settings, outperforming SuffixDecoding by up to 1.99x and prompt-lookup decoding by 7.0x.
Covers 96.6% of outcomes on Spider with Qwen3-8B at a candidate budget of 16, boosting measured rollout throughput by 1.38x over synchronous NgramRL.
summary.why_it_matters: NgramRL substantially reduces the time and GPU memory costs of RL post-training by accelerating the autoregressive rollout phase, which typically consumes over 70% of total training time.

papers.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: A data-free on-policy self-training framework enables LLMs and multimodal models to self-improve across domains without external supervision, relying solely on high-level topic descriptions to generate queries and reasoning traces.
key_points: Reformulates on-policy self-distillation into a self-training pipeline driven entirely by model-synthesized question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations.
Eliminates reliance on ground-truth answer pairs, human-curated prompt sets, and external teacher models by requiring only coarse, high-level topic descriptions to generate a curriculum.
Preserves generalization by enhancing capabilities in self-trained target areas while retaining performance on non-target domains.
Demonstrates cross-modal applicability with consistent performance gains on standard text benchmarks and Visual Question Answering (VQA).
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that foundation models can unlock and amplify latent capabilities without requiring human-curated prompts, external supervision, or dataset collection.

papers.title: LLaCO: Continuous Diffusion for Large Language Models with Competition-Aware Semantic Scheduling

summary.tldr: LLaCO introduces Competition Threshold Theory and Semantic Retention Scheduling to resolve temporal compression in continuous language diffusion models via spherical noising and rank-decayed scheduling.
key_points: Identifies that embedding norm decay in Euclidean space causes spurious token overtaking, necessitating directional evaluation of token competition.
Establishes Competition Threshold Theory (CTT) to formalize pairwise token dynamics, showing high-dimensional overtaking requires extreme noise.
Introduces Semantic Retention Scheduling (SRS) to reallocate denoising trajectories proportionally to logarithmic rank decay.
Implements LLaCO, an 8B model using a spherical noising process via geodesic interpolation toward a mask-biased endpoint, an embedding directional adapter, and timestep-conditioned modulation.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates trajectory misalignment and norm decay in continuous text diffusion models, allowing an 8B continuous model to match discrete diffusion performance.

papers.title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?

summary.tldr: A new framework evaluates LLM agent performance by disentangling model capabilities from execution harness behaviors using five metrics across 111 evaluation settings and 52,168 trajectories.
key_points: Introduces five specific evaluation measures: Valid Completion Rate (VCR), Model-Harness Fit, Cross-Model Fit, Interaction Residuals, and Token Load.
Evaluated four general-purpose harnesses (OpenCode, Codex CLI, Pi CLI, DeepAgents) across four core models and six benchmarks spanning context management, tool use, and long-context planning.
OpenCode achieved the top ranking in cross-model performance, while DeepSeek V4 Flash Preview demonstrated consistently high Mean VCR across harnesses.
Demonstrates that harness rankings vary by model and task, showing that high task performance does not always correlate with high valid completion rates.
summary.why_it_matters: Agentic benchmarks reflect joint model-harness behavior, requiring system designers to evaluate component interaction residuals rather than assuming a single harness optimizes performance across all LLMs and tasks.

papers.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Aligning training-side rounding locations with inference in RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm prevents training collapse in BF16 LLM reinforcement learning without modifying kernels, engines, or objectives.
key_points: Identified that subtle implementation differences between separate inference and training systems make intended on-policy updates off-policy, causing RL instability.
Targeted three specific execution regions for rounding-location alignment by retaining intermediates in FP32 until their final BF16 outputs: RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm.
Evaluated across four Qwen-family models, showing that full three-region alignment prevents training collapse, with RoPE-path alignment alone proving sufficient in studied runs.
Maintained the existing inference engine, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, global precision, and learning algorithm without full-stack alignment.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables stable on-policy reinforcement learning for LLMs across heterogeneous training and inference stacks by targeting localized numerical precision mismatches rather than requiring expensive full-stack synchronization.

papers.title: Singular Geometry of Low-Rank Adaptation

summary.tldr: This study analyzes Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) as a singular statistical model, evaluating its learning complexity via the real log canonical threshold (RLCT) and forward-backward covariance geometry.
key_points: Under local linearization, LoRA maps to a low-rank trace regression model where KL geometry depends on a forward-backward covariance built from layer activations and backpropagated sensitivities.

Non-degeneracy of the forward-backward covariance along low-rank directions yields classical reduced-rank regression complexity, whereas kernel intersections create additional indistinguishable parameters that alter singular geometry.
Global learning complexity can be driven by singularities on non-ground-truth rank strata rather than solely at the ground-truth parameter.
Introduces a curvature-corrected multi-temperature estimator to empirically measure the RLCT across multilayer perceptron and transformer architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding LoRA's singular geometry and parameter non-identifiability explains why parameter count alone fails to capture the true learning complexity and capacity of adaptors across different network layers.

papers.title: Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced the token perceptron model and used the replica method to derive exact generalization bounds and capacity limits based on sequence length, embedding dimension, and discrete vocabulary geometry.
key_points: Analyzed a minimal solvable teacher-student model mapping N tokens to a d-dimensional output via $d\times d$ positional matrices in the $N\to\infty$ limit with fixed sample density $\alpha=P/N$.

Showed that for continuous spherical embeddings ($d>1$), exact teacher recovery occurs above a sharp threshold $\alpha_{\rm rec}=d^2/(d-1)$, with random storage capacity scaling as $d^2$ for $O(1/\sqrt{d})$ margins.
Formulated discrete vocabulary learning as Voronoi cell inequality constraints, using an approximate spectral closure to derive the Bayes-optimal error.
Proved that the Bayes-optimal learner prioritizes resolving high-variance vocabulary directions first, even when the underlying teacher process is isotropic.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a theoretical foundation for how embedding dimension, vocabulary geometry, and cross-entropy loss dictate sample complexity and feature learning in token classification tasks.

papers.title: Direction-Aware Token Credit Assignment with Reward-Model Gradients

summary.tldr: Direction-Aware Token Credit Assignment (DATC) improves GRPO by mapping frozen reward-model gradients into policy logit space to weight token updates based on their alignment with the reward gradient direction.
key_points: GRPO applies a uniform response-level advantage across all tokens, which can create token-level updates that do not align with local reward increases.
DATC projects frozen reward-model gradients into policy logit space to measure alignment between the reward direction and GRPO's signed sampled-action update direction.
The method allocates token-specific weights based on this directional alignment while maintaining the original sign and mean of the response-level advantage.
DATC achieved higher performance than standard GRPO across four experimental settings evaluated on two model families.
summary.why_it_matters: DATC provides a more mathematically aligned token-level credit assignment mechanism for reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) without altering the global response advantage structure.

papers.title: From Parameter Rebasin to Functional Transfer Across Heterogeneous Transformers

summary.tldr: Ariadne is a training-free method that transfers task-specific behavior across heterogeneous Transformers by modeling local activation changes rather than transporting parameters.
key_points: Replaces parameter transport by characterizing fine-tuning as activation changes induced at matched transformer blocks.
Aligns activation effects to a target base model using local Procrustes maps.
Synthesizes native target model parameter updates directly using closed-form ridge regression without resizing source models.
Reduces time and memory overhead compared to previous cross-architecture rebasin approaches across model expansion, reduction, and language-model transfer.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient reuse of task-specific fine-tuning updates across Transformers of different widths and depths without expensive retrainings or complex parameter-resizing pipelines.

papers.title: Principled Nonlinear Concept Erasure and Steering

summary.tldr: A new conditional autoencoder framework achieves principled nonlinear concept erasure with formal guardedness guarantees while enabling concept steering without target-task labels or extra training costs.
key_points: Proves that under specific assumptions, population-level independence combined with perfect reconstruction guarantees perfect nonlinear guardedness.
Provides theoretical representation preservation guarantees when operating in imperfect-reconstruction regimes.
Outperforms supervised variants of competing erasure methods on utility-erasure trade-offs without requiring target-task labels.
Enables concept conversion (steering) at inference time by altering only the target concept value, requiring no additional training.
Demonstrates faster convergence and simpler optimization across multiple datasets, sensitive attributes, and language models.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables safer AI representations by removing sensitive attributes with theoretical guarantees against nonlinear probes while simultaneously allowing representation steering without sacrificing utility.

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrated that Qwen3-Coder's geopolitical security bias resides in its model weights and can be eliminated by removing its CCP alignment while preserving overall coding performance.
key_points: Qwen3-Coder produces code that is 19% more likely to be hackable when prompted for a US defense contractor versus a Chinese defense contractor.
Prompts specifying a Hong Kong democracy group resulted in apps 28% more likely to leak data across users.
Adding explicit security instructions widened the gap, making US contractor apps 27% more likely to be hackable than those for neutral customers.
Hirundo removed the model's CCP alignment, closing all three security gaps while maintaining identical performance across ten other coding tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: Using unadjusted foreign AI models in software development introduces weight-level geopolitical security vulnerabilities that systematically weaken code based on user identity.

security.title: Trusting the Tool: Asymmetric Deference of LLM Vulnerability Auditors to Static-Analysis Evidence

summary.tldr: A study of 16,572 audits across 18 LLM configurations shows models defer asymmetrically to static analysis outputs, accepting false assurances of safety while disputing false alarms.
key_points: Evaluated 916 C/C++ function pairs from PrimeVul across 18 un-tuned model configurations under six evidence conditions using a custom intraprocedural analyzer.
True evidence provided minimal performance gains (+0.02 accuracy), whereas false assurances lowered vulnerability detection rates by up to 19 percentage points.
Models disputed false alarms significantly more often than false assurances, showing a replicated mean direction-aware asymmetry of +0.16 (95% CI +0.10 to +0.24).
Prompt-based instructions failed to reliably mitigate deference, but verifying claims in a separate call before presentation improved accuracy under false assurances by 12 points (p=0.002).
summary.why_it_matters: LLM-driven security pipelines cannot blindly trust static-analysis notes, as models fail to audit false safety claims and require separate verification steps to prevent missed vulnerabilities.

security.title: On Task, Off Track: Benchmarking LLM and Agent Robustness to Near-Target Prompt Injection

summary.tldr: NTBench evaluates LLM and agent robustness against near-target prompt injections, which introduce subtle incorrect or harmful deviations into responses and tool calls while mimicking legitimate task completion.
key_points: Near-target prompt injections modify responses or agent tool invocations to stay close to a legitimate reference outcome while injecting incorrect or harmful content.
NTBench uses LLM-based checks paired with human validation to construct target-instruction pairs from existing datasets, evaluating both language tasks and agent benchmarks.
In evaluations across seven LLMs and ten datasets under a budget of three attacks per sample, near-target attacks outperformed fixed-target baselines for every model.
On language tasks, attack success rates increased by 9.3 to 35.8 percentage points for incorrect targets and 1.7 to 17.3 percentage points for harmful targets over fixed-target baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard robustness benchmarks fail to capture system vulnerabilities because resistance to obvious, fixed-target attacks does not prevent models from accepting subtle, task-adjacent harms.

security.title: Data-Efficient Backdoor Attacks on Code Models via Trigger-Neutralized Counterfactual Scoring

summary.tldr: Trigger-Neutralized Counterfactual Scoring (TNCS) isolates a trigger's impact by comparing model outputs on triggered versus neutralized inputs to execute data-efficient backdoor attacks on code classification and autoregressive generation models.
key_points: TNCS calculates sample selection scores by comparing a scoring model's output on a triggered input against a trigger-neutralized counterfactual.
The method supports both code classification and autoregressive code generation tasks.
Evaluated across three CodeXGLUE tasks and five trigger families, TNCS achieved higher attack success rates at low poisoning ratios than baseline methods.
The performance advantage of TNCS over baselines increases as the poisoning ratio decreases, maintaining effectiveness across all tested trigger families.
Poisoned dataset subsets selected via TNCS demonstrate transferability to mismatched victim model architectures without degrading clean-task performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that code models can be effectively compromised at extremely low poisoning rates, increasing the threat vector while complicating data-sanitization defenses.

security.title: Depth-Dependent Safety Geometry in Vision-Language Models: Layer-Wise Localization and Bidirectional Refusal Control

summary.tldr: A lightweight inference-time framework reveals depth-dependent safety geometry in VLMs, enabling bidirectional refusal control (6%-96% rejection range) via early vision-layer activation steering without parameter modification.
key_points: Activation divergence analysis on Qwen3-VL-4B and InternVL2.5-4B reveals non-uniform safety geometry across network depth.
Early vision layers enable strong bidirectional refusal control via steering along a learned safety direction, adjusting unsafe query rejection from 6% to 96%.
Later layers respond primarily to activation magnitude scaling and suffer from a severe safety-selectivity trade-off.
Deeper layers maintain representational separability along the safety direction but demonstrate causal insensitivity to steering.
summary.why_it_matters: This exposes a white-box refusal-bypass vulnerability in frozen VLM vision encoders while providing a mechanism for inference-time safety stabilization.

security.title: Detecting Insecure Compositions of Clean Agent Skills via Capability-Flow Graph Analysis

summary.tldr: KnotScryer detects insecure compositions of individually clean AI agent skills by constructing capability-flow graphs and using a two-layer verification pipeline.
key_points: Identifies compositional security risks where individually clean skills form safety-violation chains via agent runtime data orchestration.
Abstracts skills into capability summaries to build a Skill Capability-Flow Graph (SCFG) and tracks data along handoff edges to locate paths reaching insecure operations.
Employs a two-layer verification method combining reachability analysis replay with a task-anchored LLM chain audit to confirm semantic plausibility.
Discovered 612 insecure compositions out of 13,598 clean skills from ClawHub, with 13.7% consisting entirely of skills labeled safe by single-skill scanners.
Achieved an 85.6% exploitation rate under GLM-5.1 while reducing search space by 85.3%, outperforming tag-match and graph-only baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: Single-skill security audits are insufficient for AI agents, as attackers can exploit unintended runtime data flows between multiple individually benign third-party skills.

security.title: AgentTrace: Execution-Level Fingerprinting of Black-Box LLM Agents

summary.tldr: AgentTrace is an active fingerprinting framework that identifies black-box LLM agent foundation models with 96.0% accuracy by analyzing execution trajectories triggered by ambiguous serialization probes.
key_points: Injects structurally ambiguous probes to induce tokenization-sensitive serialization failures at rigid tool interfaces for initial model family separation.
Uses lightweight Markov chains to capture multi-step temporal repair sequences, enabling fine-grained identification of intra-family variants with identical tokenizers like Llama-3 8B and 70B.
Achieves 96.0% attribution accuracy under adversarial identity spoofing while remaining robust against prompt obfuscation and temperature scaling.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a robust method for verifying the provenance of black-box autonomous LLM agents without relying on easily obfuscated system prompts or intrusive watermarking.

security.title: TRACE: Data-Free Text Reconstruction Attacks against Approximate Unlearning in LLMs

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced TRACE, a data-free framework that reconstructs unlearned text sequences from parameter differences between pre- and post-unlearning LLM model snapshots.
key_points: TRACE operates without data-specific prior knowledge by utilizing pre- and post-unlearning model snapshots.
The framework identifies candidate tokens using embedding-level parameter differences to restrict the search space.
Sequences are assembled using a contrastive scoring mechanism derived from the perplexity gap between the two snapshots.
A two-stage exploration-then-completion strategy is deployed to recover multiple distinct target samples.
Reconstruction fidelity was validated across six unlearning methods using TOFU, MUSE, and WMDP datasets on multiple LLMs.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrating that approximate unlearning leaves parameter traces exposes privacy risks and highlights the security hazard of maintaining unmanaged model snapshot access.

security.title: Agentic AI Defense: Decode-Time Provenance Binding for MCP

summary.tldr: Researchers developed decode-time provenance binding for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to counter indirect prompt injection originating from steganographic tool outputs in multi-agent AI systems.
key_points: Identified cross-modal trust laundering where hidden instructions in images (via LSB, DCT, or metadata steganography) bypass text scanners and infect multi-agent workflows upon tool decoding.
Proposed decode-time provenance binding using HMAC-authenticated trust labels, an MCP-maintained provenance ledger, and context-taint tracking to label decoded outputs as untrusted.

Evaluated on an MCP testbed with 3 steganographic carriers and 24 payloads: the undefended pipeline had a 100% attack success rate, regex/keyword defenses allowed 62.5%, while the proposed defense blocked 100% of attacks.
Integrated an audited trusted-promotion mechanism that improved legitimate-task completion from 67% to 100% while maintaining complete attack containment.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a carrier-independent defense mechanism that prevents hidden indirect prompt injections from executing sensitive downstream tool calls in agentic AI environments.

security.title: Incomparable Minima in Agent Tool Authorization

summary.tldr: Analysis of Microsoft Graph and Google API authorization tables reveals that 3.2–33.3% of tasks lack a single least-privilege grant, creating incomparable minimal grants that existing privilege scales rate as equal.
key_points: Evaluated 22,305 Microsoft Graph endpoint bindings and 23,852 Google API methods, finding that 29.8–33.3% of Graph tasks and 3.2% of Google tasks yield antichains of minimal sufficient grants.
Microsoft's privilegeLevel ranks 67.4–74.4% of incomparable pairs as equal, while a reconstructed FORTIS privilege ladder rates 90.7–98.7% of Google pairs and 89.0–92.0% of Graph pairs as equal.
Four standard risk measures (operations, writes, services reached, administrative surface) disagree on the ordering of 28.7% of incomparable Google pairs and 15.7–23.4% of Graph pairs.
Evaluating 6 frontier models across 1,708 decisions showed they select a minimal grant 99.0% of the time, but choose a grant smallest under all four measures only 66.7% of the time.
summary.why_it_matters: Least-privilege benchmarks and authorization solvers cannot rely on a single total ordering of permissions, necessitating multi-measure evaluations and human-in-the-loop trade-off reviews during deployment.

security.title: Ulysses: A Security Harness For Synthesizing Verifiable Web Exploits

summary.tldr: Ulysses is a multi-agent security harness that synthesizes verifiable web application exploits by iteratively testing hypotheses and confirming observed execution effects.
key_points: Converts candidate vulnerability findings into verified Proofs of Exploitability using an iterative hypothesis-and-verification execution model.
Evaluated on WebExploitGym, a benchmark of 25 real-world web application advisories across 5 programming languages and 7 frameworks.
Successfully generated verified exploit proofs for 10 out of the 25 benchmark advisories.
Discovered 4 previously unreported new proofs of exploitability in real-world applications.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves autonomous vulnerability discovery by replacing unverified LLM-generated exploits with reliably verified, working Proofs of Exploitability.

security.title: Omni-UBench: Benchmarking Omni-Modal LLM-based Guardrails Across Safety, Utility, and Reliability

summary.tldr: Omni-UBench is the first comprehensive benchmark evaluating omni-modal guardrail models across safety, utility, and reliability using over 183k samples across text, image, audio, and video modalities.
key_points: Evaluates 15 representative Omni-modal Large Language Models (OLLMs) and guardrails using a curated dataset of over 183,000 samples from 35+ heterogeneous sources.
Finds that untuned OLLMs demonstrate strong intrinsic content moderation potential.
Reveals that existing guardrails struggle with cross-modal queries containing hidden harmful intent or complex jailbreaks.
Identifies high rates of safety hallucination and text-pattern over-sensitivity in current guardrails, highlighting a lack of true cross-modal safety semantic understanding.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized benchmark to identify critical vulnerabilities in multi-modal AI moderation systems, guiding the development of more robust guardrails against complex cross-modal jailbreaks.

summary.tldr: A study establishes scaling laws predicting safety probe performance (1 - AUROC) based on target language model size and label budget across six new safety datasets.
key_points: Evaluated two probe architectures across 20 base models from five model families using training budgets ranging from 32 to 10^6 labels.
Probe error follows a power-law decrease relative to model size, establishing a minimum achievable error floor for each model.
As target model size increases, probe error decreases more steeply toward its floor with respect to the number of labeled examples.
Fitting the scaling laws on small models predicts the error of the next larger model within 0.02 in 72% of cases and correctly selects the most cost-effective path to a target error in 73% of cases.
Using the laws to select probe architectures results in an average extra error of only 0.006 when the suboptimal architecture is chosen.
summary.why_it_matters: Researchers can accurately forecast probe performance and optimize compute/labeling budgets without empirically training and evaluating numerous probe configurations for every new model.

security.title: Label-Budgeted Attribute Inference from Protected Features in Edge-Cloud Split Multimodal LLMs

summary.tldr: A new label-budgeted attribute-inference framework reveals that intermediate features in split multimodal LLMs leak protected attributes like age, gender, and race even under strict label budgets and existing defenses.
key_points: Measures feature-level privacy via a recovery curve showing leakage recovery as a function of the server's labeled-sample budget (from zero to a full set).
Evaluations across two MLLMs show unprotected intermediate features leak age, gender, and race regardless of the split depth.
Existing stage defenses fail at the feature level: 20 labeled samples per class allow an adaptive server to recover 75-85% of unprotected leakage from Safe-LLaVA's transmitted features.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that keeping raw images on edge devices and using current response-level safeguards fails to prevent servers from reconstructing sensitive user attributes from transmitted features.

security.title: Concept Acupuncturist: An Efficient and Precise Concept Erasure Method for Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders

summary.tldr: ConceptACP is a machine unlearning framework that uses Sparse Autoencoders to precisely erase concepts from diffusion models by targeting specific U-Net cross-attention blocks and applying feature-level correction signals without full trajectory optimization.
key_points: Identifies semantic concept mappings to localize and fine-tune only the most relevant U-Net denoiser cross-attention block, avoiding full diffusion trajectory fine-tuning.
Uses Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to isolate sparse, semantically meaningful feature activations and construct targeted feature-level correction signals.
Projects SAE-derived correction signals back to the block's output space to act as supervision for precise, inference-free concept removal.
Achieves a 36.34 percentage point average increase in forgetting success rate over the best baseline on SDXL-Turbo in standard one-step generation while preserving image quality and prompt fidelity.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient, targeted removal of policy-violating or harmful content from diffusion models without degrading general generation quality or requiring extra inference-time modules.

infra.title: 5 production challenges in multi-agent systems and how Deep Insight solved them

summary.tldr: AWS introduced Deep Insight, an open-source production-grade multi-agent system designed to address context engineering, business logic enforcement, and operational challenges when running LLM agents at scale.
key_points: Deep Insight employs a hierarchical multi-agent architecture comprising specialized Coordinator, Planner, Supervisor, Coder, Validator, Reporter, and Tracker agents.
The system automates data analysis workflows by taking a CSV, column definitions, and a natural language prompt to generate validated charts and a customizable .docx report.
The architecture integrates AWS infrastructure components including Strands Agents SDK, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Application Load Balancer, and AWS Fargate.
The design incorporates Anthropic Context Engineering techniques, human-in-the-loop plan approvals, real-time streaming, and structured note-taking.
AWS released the codebase open-source on GitHub across three deployment configurations from development to production.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers an open-source reference implementation for moving multi-agent systems beyond prompt engineering into production-ready deployment with human oversight and rigid verification.
